Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are well‑known for offering vegetarian (and often vegan) options. All of them are located in or near downtown, so you’ll have plenty of other dining choices nearby. | Restaurant | Address | Phone | Website | Vegetarian Highlights | |------------|---------|-------|---------|------------------------| | **Siam Thai Bistro** | 1110 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 555‑1234 | [siamthai.com](https://www.siamthai.com) | • **Vegetarian Pad Thai** (no egg, tofu instead)
• **Vegetarian Green Curry** (tofu, mixed veggies)
• **Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup** (no fish sauce, extra lemongrass)
• **Fresh Spring Rolls** (vegetable & tofu) | | **Thai Orchid** | 2001 N Clark St, Chicago, IL 60614 | (312) 555‑5678 | [thaiochard.com](https://www.thaiochard.com) | • **Vegetarian Massaman Curry** (potato, carrot, tofu)
• **Vegetarian Pad Krapow** (tofu, basil, chili)
• **Vegetarian Papaya Salad** (no fish sauce, extra lime)
• **Vegetarian Fried Rice** (no egg, tofu) | | **Baan Thai** | 1700 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 555‑9012 | [baanthai.com](https://www.baanthai.com) | • **Vegetarian Red Curry** (tofu, bell pepper, bamboo shoots)
• **Vegetarian Stir‑Fried Noodles** (no egg, tofu)
• **Vegetarian Satay Skewers** (tofu, peanut sauce)
• **Vegetarian Mango Sticky Rice** (vegan dessert) | | **Thai Kitchen** | 400 N Clark St, Chicago, IL 60654 | (312) 555‑3456 | [thaikitchen.com](https://www.thaikitchen.com) | • **Vegetarian Panang Curry** (tofu, sweet potato)
• **Vegetarian Pad See Ew** (no egg, tofu)
• **Vegetarian Tom Kha Soup** (coconut milk, mushrooms)
• **Vegetarian Spring Rolls** (vegan) | | **Siam Square** | 1200 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 555‑7890 | [siamsquare.com](https://www.siamsquare.com) | • **Vegetarian Green Curry** (tofu, eggplant, bamboo shoots)
• **Vegetarian Pad Thai** (no egg, tofu)
• **Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup** (no fish sauce, extra lime)
• **Vegetarian Fried Rice** (no egg, tofu) | ### How to Order * **Online Delivery** – Most of these restaurants partner with UberEats, DoorDash, or Grubhub. Check their website or the delivery app for vegetarian menus. * **Phone Reservations** – If you’re planning a larger group or want to confirm vegetarian options, call ahead. The staff are usually very accommodating. * **In‑Person** – All restaurants have a “Vegetarian” or “Vegan” option listed on their menus. If you’re unsure, ask the server for a vegetarian-friendly dish. ### Tips for Vegetarian Diners 1. **Ask About Fish Sauce** – Many Thai dishes contain fish sauce. Request it to be omitted or replaced with soy sauce or a vegetarian alternative. 2. **Check for Egg** – Pad Thai and fried rice often contain eggs. Ask for “egg‑free” versions. 3. **Extra Veggies** – You can always add extra vegetables or tofu to make a dish more vegetarian-friendly. 4. **Desserts** – Mango sticky rice is typically vegan, but some places add condensed milk. Ask for a dairy‑free version if needed. Enjoy your Thai culinary adventure in Chicago! If you’d like more detailed menus or specific dish recommendations, let me know.
